did_you_know.text: Did you know? Joab realized that David’s heart was still with Absalom, so he looked for a way to move the king to bring his son back.
Did you know? Joab chose a wise woman from Tekoa and instructed her to put on mourning clothes and present David with a carefully planned story.
Did you know? In the woman’s parable, her only son is in danger of blood revenge from the family, and she fears that both her heir and her husband’s name will be wiped out.
Did you know? David swore to the woman that no harm would come to her son, saying, “As the LORD lives, not a hair of your son’s head will fall to the ground.”

Did you know? The woman from Tekoa compares life to water poured out on the ground, which cannot be gathered up again, emphasizing the finality of death; yet she also reminds David that God does not want the banished person to remain lost.
Did you know? David recognized that Joab was behind the woman’s words, and she praised the king’s wisdom as being like “the wisdom of the angel of God.”
Did you know? Joab brought Absalom from Geshur to Jerusalem, but David ordered him to return to his own house and did not allow him to see the king’s face.
Did you know? Scripture describes Absalom as exceptionally handsome, with no blemish from the sole of his foot to the crown of his head.
Did you know? Absalom’s hair was so heavy that after it was cut, he weighed it; Scripture gives its weight as two hundred shekels by the royal standard.
Did you know? After Joab refused to come to him, Absalom ordered his barley field to be set on fire; this prompted Joab to come and speak with him.
